sections.title: Because
sections.content: *Mert* means "because". It joins a reason to what you said, and the reason is a short sentence of its own: *Levest kérek, mert éhes vagyok.* Always write a comma before *mert*. To ask for a reason use *miért* (why): *Miért nem kérsz levest?* The answer can start with *mert*: *Mert túl csípős.*

sections.title: Why? Because...
rows: I'd like soup because I am hungry.
I'd like water because I am thirsty.

items.spanish: Nem kérek húst, mert vegetáriánus vagyok.
items.english: I do not want meat because I am a vegetarian.

items.spanish: Nem kérem a levest, mert túl csípős.
items.english: I won't take the soup because it is too spicy.

items.spanish: Salátát kérek, mert nem vagyok éhes.
items.english: I'd like a salad because I am not hungry.
I would like water because I am thirsty.

sections.content: The comma comes before *mert*, not after it: *Vizet kérek, mert szomjas vagyok.* *Miért* asks the question, *mert* gives the answer; they are not interchangeable.
